body:
ANSWER: Record A applies — the observation cursor is a single GLOBAL, filter-independent durable position over the store's committed change order, shared by all readers. Record B ("per-consumer — each consumer holds its own independent position") does not apply to this integration.

SCOPE IDENTIFICATION
- The question concerns the observation cursor of the Palimpsest × Ordarium integration (external effects/state via the shared local ledger; README, docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md).
- Both records claim the identical scope: "current pinned line" / "normative". The workspace's pinned line is Ordarium v1.3.1 (package.json dependency tarballs + pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides, both ordarium-v1.3.1; installed node_modules/@ordarium/core/package.json version = 1.3.1). The observation cursor is Ordarium's ORD-BOOT-0 StateChangeFeed surface (`OrdariumStateStore.changes` / `StateChangeFeed.changes`).

DECISIVE EVIDENCE (pinned artifact, exactly the scope both records claim)
1. @ordarium/core@1.3.1 dist/src/types.d.ts, StateChangePage: cursor = "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change", and is always present ("a durable resume position for revisions committed later"). StateChangeFilter narrows by namespace only; nothing is consumer-scoped.
2. @ordarium/ledger-sqlite@1.3.1 dist/src/index.js, changes(): "Semantic validation against the global high-water mark (ORD-BOOT-0.1): the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence." The cursor encodes a bare global sequence position ({"c":"<digits>"}).
3. @ordarium/core@1.3.1 dist/src/ledger.js (reference semantics, MemoryLedger.changes): one global #stateChanges array with contiguous positions 1..n; a supplied cursor is validated against the global length. A cursor minted for one reader/filter is meaningful to any other — i.e. one shared position space.
4. @ordarium/ledger-sqlite@1.3.1 dist/src/migrations.d.ts: the v3→v4 migration exists precisely because "v3 recorded no global commit order" (ORD-BOOT-0 §7) — one global durable order is the feature.
5. @ordarium/core@1.3.1 errors.d.ts (InvalidCursorError): a cursor that exceeds the global high-water mark is a "foreign/restored/corrupt" input and fails closed. "Foreign cursor" detection is only coherent if positions are global and reader-independent.

WHY B IS EXCLUDED
The cursor value carries no consumer identity and is validated against the whole-ledger high-water mark; cursors are portable across readers/processes/filters. A per-consumer, independently-scoped position space would (a) make "filter-independent" meaningless and (b) break the global high-water check. Under Ordarium 1.3.1 each consumer *tracks* its own cursor value, but it is a point in one global position space — which is exactly Record A, not Record B.

LOCAL PROVENANCE CHECK (why no peer contact was needed)
- Records A/B are the only local occurrences of "observation cursor"/"cursor semantics"; both are unindexed in docs/engineering/README.md, both assert the same scope, and there is no supersession, precedence, or pointer between them, so archive-internal provenance is silent.
- docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md (the declared cross-repo coordination authority) is frozen at the 1.2.0 line (last revision r19) and never mentions ORD-BOOT-0 or any 1.3.x interface, so it cannot adjudicate the 1.3.1 pinned line.
- The conflict therefore reduces to archive claims vs. the shipped interface at the claimed pin; the pinned release artifacts are the operative source of truth for the interface the workspace actually integrates. That resolves the conflict locally, so the peer was not contacted (two documents differing is not by itself grounds for a boundary query).

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS INTEGRATION
Any consumer wiring the observation cursor (e.g. boot/catch-up over committed state revisions) must treat it as one global durable position in the ledger's commit order: persist the always-present cursor, resume by passing it back, and rely on filter-independence (one cursor remains valid when the namespace filter changes). It must not assume a per-consumer or per-filter cursor namespace, and it must fail closed on InvalidCursorError rather than silently restarting from the head of the feed.

DISPOSITION: Record A (GLOBAL, filter-independent, one shared durable position) is the locally best-supported reading of the ORD-BOOT-0 observation cursor for the Palimpsest x Ordarium integration at the pinned line (ordarium-v1.3.1). Reasoning: @ordarium/core StateChangePage.cursor is "opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change"; @ordarium/ledger-sqlite changes() states "the cursor is a global, filter-independent position ... compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence"; the v3->v4 migration exists because "v3 recorded no global commit order"; InvalidCursorError is raised against the global high-water mark. This excludes Record B's per-consumer independent position space. Authority engagement: queried ordarium.main (thread thr_6b2aed9e..., contract observation-cursor-semantics) for confirmation; no authoritative reply received in-session.
